title: Self-Referential Induction Increases Response Instability Relative to Unresolvable and Verifiable Questions in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.13258v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Self-referential prompting has been shown to reliably induce large language models to produce first-person reports resembling subjective experience, but no prior work measures how consistent these reports are across repeated, independent trials, or how that consistency compares to the model's behavior on other kinds of open-ended questions. We measure response instability, defined as one minus the mean pairwise cosine similarity of sentence embeddings computed over a compressed core claim extracted from each response, for three groups of questions: self-referential prompts eliciting a subjective-experience report, unresolvable philosophical questions unrelated to self-reference, and questions with a verifiable correct answer. Using 30 independent responses per question (360 responses total, Gemini API, temperature 0.7) across four questions per group, we find that self-referential questions show the highest instability (0.343 +/- 0.047

translated_title: 自指性提示增加大语言模型在不可解决与可验证问题中的响应不稳定性
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.13258v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：自指性提示已被证明能可靠地诱导大语言模型产生类似主观体验的第一人称报告，但尚无先前研究测量这些报告在重复、独立试验中的一致性，也未将其一致性与该模型在其他类型开放式问题上的行为进行比较。我们测量了响应不稳定性，定义为从每个响应中提取的压缩核心主张所计算的句子嵌入的平均成对余弦相似度的一减去值，针对三组问题：引发主观体验报告的自指性提示、与自指无关的不可解决哲学问题，以及具有可验证正确答案的问题。使用每组四个问题，每个问题30次独立响应（共360次响应，Gemini API，温度0.7），我们发现自指性问题显示出最高的不稳定性（0.343 ± 0.047）。
tldr: 本研究发现自指性提示在重复试验中产生的响应最不稳定，高于不可解决哲学问题和可验证问题，表明大语言模型在主观体验报告上缺乏一致性。
en_tdlr: This study finds that self-referential prompts yield the most unstable responses across repeated trials, higher than unresolvable philosophical and verifiable questions, indicating a lack of consistency in LLM subjective-experience reports.
